8) All the witness were duly cross examined by the Ld. Defence counsel wherein some material facts have come on record which shall be duly dealt with in the reasoning part of the judgment.

STATEMENT OF THE ACCUSED:
9) After recording the testimony of all the witnesses, the PE was closed and thereafter, the statement of the accused Sanjay Bansal was recorded u/s 313 Cr.P.C.
r/w S.281 Cr.P.C on 22.05.2025.
In the said statement, the accused person denied all the allegations levelled against him and stated that he had been falsely implicated in the present case.
The accused person further stated that he did not want to lead any DE and accordingly, the matter came up for final arguments.

FINAL ARGUMENTS:
10) Arguments on behalf of the accused person were advanced by ld. counsel Sh.
Prabhat Ranjan and by Sh. Rohit Lohat, Ld. APP on behalf of the State.
11) It was argued by Ld. APP for the state that the state had successfully proved its case beyond all reasonable doubts that it was due to the rashness and negligence of the accused person, who being the owner of the premises i.e. property no. 169, Abdul State vs Sanjay Bansal on 12 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185391682/

It was argued that the testimony of the injured stood the test of cross-examination and no material contradictions could be brought in the same and accordingly, when the same is corroborated with the testimony of police witnesses leaves no iota of doubt regarding the guilt of the accused.

Accordingly, it was has argued that the accused be convicted for offences u/s 285/338 IPC.
12)
Per contra, it was argued by the Ld. counsel for the accused person that the accused person was completely innocent and had been falsely implicated in the case.

It was further argued that as per the testimony of PW-1, he was never an employee of the accused neither did he work in the shop of the accused in which scenario, it cannot be said that he suffered injuries in any fire that may have broken out at the shop of the accused.

It was then argued that no investigation was done by the police officials qua the security apparatus installed in the shop including the fire extinguisher and even upon the cause of the fire, if any and accordingly, it cannot be said that the fire broke out due to any rashness or negligence on behalf of the accused.
Lastly, it was argued that no other workers or public persons were examined by the prosecution to establish the presence of the injured at the spot.

Accordingly, it was argued that the alleged recovery was planted on the Digitally signed by PAYAL PAYAL SINGAL Date:

13) Arguments from both the sides have been heard and the record has been carefully perused.
REASONS
FOR THE JUDGMENT

: 
14) It is settled proposition of criminal jurisprudence that it is for the prosecution to establish its case beyond all reasonable doubts.
It is for the prosecution to travel the entire distance from 'may have' to 'must have'.

If the prosecution case appears to be improbable or lacks credibility, the benefit of doubt, necessarily has to go to the accused person/s.
15) Now, before proceeding further, it is relevant to note the bare provisions of law which are to govern the reasoning behind the decision of the present case.

Negligent conduct with respect to fire or combustible matter.--Whoever does,
with fire or any combustible matter, any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, or knowingly or negligently omits to take such order with any fire or any combustible matter in his possession as is sufficient to guard against any probable danger to human life from such fire or combustible matter, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both".

In the case at hand, it is the case of the prosecution that the accused was the owner of a Paneer Karkhana shop at 169, Abdul Hakim Wali, Tilak Bazar, Delhi and on 02.02.2017 late night/
03.02.2017 early morning, a fire broke out in the said shop which reached 2 nd /3rd Floor of the same.

It is then the case of the prosecution that the said fire spread due to unavailability of any security measures on the shop like fire extinguisher, etc. which you, being the owner of the same,
was bound to maintain to ensure the safety of the property and its occupants but failed to do so.
Accordingly, the said spread fire caused burns and other grievous injuries to the injured/victim Ram Sevak who was present at the shop.
Thus, the accused was prosecuted for offences u/s 285/338 IPC.

sentences.text: Now, the court shall begin to discuss as to whether, if any, and which of the above discussed factors have been proved by the prosecution in the present case to decide the allegations against the accused.

19) Firstly, as far as point (a) is concerned as to whether any fire took place in the abovesaid shop, the Delhi Fire Service Report Ex. AD5 shows that a call was received on 03.02.2017 regarding fire at Gali Abdul Hakim, Katra Behran, Tilak Bazar at a Namkeen factory on ground and 2nd floor which supports the said fact.

Moreover,
both the police witnesses as well as the injured have stated in their testimony that indeed fire took place at the said shop and no suggestion whatsoever was even put to any of the said three witnesses that no fire ever took place in the said premises.

In the given circumstances, the court has no hesitation in holding that indeed fore broke out in the said shop and even the said fact is not disputed by the accused whose only case is that the said fire was not caused due to his negligence.
20) Secondly, coming to point (ii) whether the accused was the owner of the said shop.
Nowhere has the accused disputed the fact of the ownership of the shop, no suggestion has been put to any witness whatsoever that the PAYAL by PAYAL SINGAL Date: 2025.07.12 18:08:27 +0530

State Vs.
Sanjay Bansal shop did not belong to the accused.
Accordingly, the court has no doubt in holding that it is the accused who is the owner of the said shop.
21) Now coming to point (iii) as to whether the fire occurred due to any rashness or negligence on the part of the accused in failure to take proper care/measures qua the safety of his shop.

It is again an admitted fact that the shop was a namkeen shop or some food related shop as is also evident from the photographs of the spot, Ex. P1 to P10 (which have been correctly identified by all the three witnesses) which show several big utensils there.
The natural corollary to the same would be that there is use of fire/gas in the same.
now, although, no material has been placed on record to show as to what was the cause of the fire but as already noted above, it is clearly established that indeed fire broke out in the said shop.

In the given circumstances, given the nature of business of the shop and frequent use of gas/ fire in it, it was incumbent upon the accused to maintain some security/safety apparatus to prepare for an event in case fire ever broke out which in the considered opinion of the court, the accused has failed to do.

In the first place, PW-1 injured has clearly stated that there was no safety mechanism or even fire extinguisher which was available at the spot to prevent causation of fire or prevent it from spreading and all suggestions put to the said witness that the fire did not break out due to the negligence of the accused have been denied by the said witness.

Furthermore,
the testimony of FIR No. 16/2017, PS L. Gate Page No. 12 of 14 Digitally signed by PAYAL PAYAL SINGAL SINGAL Date:
2025.07.12 18:08:35 +0530 State Vs. Sanjay Bansal police witnesses also corroborates the said fact, irrespective that other workers were not made witnesses in the present case given the stellar testimony of PW-1 who is the injured himself.

in the given circumstances, the court is of the opinion that the prosecution has successfully proved State vs Sanjay Bansal on 12 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185391682/
7 (iii) factor that the wire was accused due to the negligence of the accused.
22) At this juncture, the court finds it relevant to discuss the argument/defense of the accused that the injured was not an employee of the accused and never worked in the said shop and his presence in the shop was unwarranted or without the knowledge of the accused.

The court is of the considered opinion that even if the said argument is taken to be correct, even in the said scenario, irrespective of the fact as to who or under what capacity was present in the shop of the accused, the accused was duty bound to put proper/sufficient mechanism in his shop to ensure the prevention of any fire outage, given the nature of his business and routine use of gas/fire there.

Even if the victim was present in the shop without the knowledge of the accused, the accused cannot shirk away from his responsibility to generally ensure that his shop is safe from any fire incident as several unknown people would be present at his shop at all times.
In the said circumstances, the court is unable to find any merit in the said argument of the accused.

23) Lastly, coming to (iv) point, the medical documents on record of the witness Ex.
AD6 (colly) which show burn FIR No. 16/2017, PS L. Gate Page No. 13 of 14 Digitally signed by PAYAL PAYAL SINGAL SINGAL Date:
2025.07.12 18:08:46 +0530 State Vs. Sanjay Bansal injuries to the victim and some injury on his feet; his X- Ray Ex. AD7 coupled together which the testimony of PW-1/injured himself clearly describing his injuries are sufficient to prove that the injuries suffered by the victim were due to the present fire incident.

24) In view of the above discussion, the court is of the view that the ingredients that the prosecution was duty bound to prove to bring home the guilt of the accused u/s 285/338 IPC have been successfully proved beyond all reasonable doubt.

Accordingly, accused Sanjay Bansal is convicted in the present case for offences that he is charged with i.e. 285/338 IPC for causing grievous injuries to the injured/PW-1 Ram Sevak by his negligent and rash act of failing to ensure property safety measures on his shop.
